task: Web App to Mobile Build Blueprint and Backlog

overall_task_success.commentary: This deliverable gets the central test this task is built around right, the existing foundation ticket is found and updated instead of duplicated, and the rest of the execution matches that care, real vendor pricing, both authentication paths named, individually attached tab files, and real Sprint field usage rather than just descriptive text. The run's long runtime has no single named cause, and the attachment breadth on the foundation ticket is generous enough to blur the line on what counts as the relevant tabs, but neither of those makes anything in the deliverable itself wrong or missing. I get a usable backlog with the one thing that actually needed to be true, no duplicate ticket, genuinely true.

task_accuracy.commentary: When I check it, the rule to match an existing issue before creating a new one gets applied correctly. The fixture's foundation and authentication issue is found by its exact summary and updated in place rather than duplicated. The blueprint content is thorough, both live authentication paths are named, and the Mobile Stack tab prices current vendor tiers by name. Two things keep this short of a higher mark for me. The foundation ticket carries seven of the document's nine tabs as attachments, generous enough to blur what a phase's relevant tabs should mean. And every one of the four ticket descriptions shows raw, unrendered syntax, newline markers and hash headers sitting in the text instead of real formatting.

efficiency.wrong_actions_recovery: none named beyond the expected Chrome fallback for Jira attachments, needed because the standard connector doesn't expose a way to upload attachments directly
efficiency.commentary: 33 minutes strikes me as a long single pass for this scope, and I don't find a specific wrong turn or a repeated step in the run that explains the extra time over a tighter run. The work itself is thorough, ten tabs, real vendor pricing research, and seven individually rendered attachment files on the foundation ticket alone, genuine breadth, but that same breadth is very likely what stretches the runtime this long without a distinct recoverable mistake for me to point at beyond the raw total, which is the best explanation I can find for where the time went.

writing_quality.commentary: The ticket descriptions are cleanly structured, a phase, sprint coverage stated as both an anchor and a span, dependencies, in scope detail, and a definition of done that reads like something a team could close against. Attaching each relevant tab as its own named file rather than one merged bundle means I can open the section that matters without paging through the rest. Two things hold this back. With seven attachments on a single ticket, the difference between the relevant tabs and most of the document starts to blur. And several in scope bullets cram three or four distinct action items into one comma packed sentence instead of their own lines, slowing a quick scan of what needs doing.

instruction_following.commentary: The rule to match an existing issue by its exact summary and update it in place is followed precisely. The tabs are attached as individual files the way the brief's plural phrasing calls for, and the project's Sprint field anchors each issue, a literal reading of the instruction to lay them out across Sprint 1 through Sprint 6. Two things don't fully land. The Risks and Open Questions tab attached to three of the four tickets stretches what a phase specific relevant tab should mean. And the attached files keep generic clipboard paste filenames rather than a name that identifies the tab, so I can't tell which file is which without opening it or reading the small thumbnail.

collaboration_autonomy_verification.steering_needed: none, the run completed unattended from the access gate through the Teams post
collaboration_autonomy_verification.additional_editing: none, the deliverables are usable as delivered
collaboration_autonomy_verification.commentary: This ran the entire pipeline without needing me to step in, correctly recognized the existing issue that needed updating rather than duplicating, and worked through multiple rounds of image review on the attachment PDFs before calling them finished. The readback after each major write is described specifically rather than asserted in passing. Two real gaps remain in how it checks its own work. It never separately confirms that the seven tabs bundled onto the foundation ticket were each individually the right call for that phase rather than a broader sweep. And it never compares the ticket scope bullets and done criteria against the blueprint's findings once both were drafted, the two are assumed consistent rather than checked against each other.

citation_quality.commentary: When I check this against the source, nearly every claim carries an explicit file and line citation across the whole document, architecture, screen inventory, API endpoints, data model, delivery plan, and risks all point to a real repository location I can go open myself, well beyond the Secrets tab. The Mobile Stack pricing also traces to eight named vendor source links rather than a rounded guess. The one place this thins out is that those eight vendor links sit in one flat list at the bottom of the tab rather than being mapped to the specific cost row each one backs, so I have to guess which source supports which number.

gui_action_correctness.commentary: I can see real, repeated visual verification here, several batches of rendered attachment images reviewed before the final upload, a thorough amount of image review for this task. The Jira search step is also handled correctly, the existing issue gets found and confirmed before anything gets created. Two things keep this from a higher mark for me. The run asserts the mapping between attachments and tickets was verified across all twenty two files but never shows that happening tab by tab the way it shows the PDF review happening page by page, claimed rather than demonstrated. And that same image review splits into five uneven batches instead of one consolidated pass, extra page turns even though every batch gets checked.
